name: SparkFun Qwiic Buzzer
description: I2C-controlled magnetic buzzer (CUI CBT-09427-SMT-TR, 2730 Hz resonant, 16 Ohm coil): an ATtiny84 running SparkFun's QwiicBuzzerFirmware plays a tone at any frequency set in Hz, for a set duration in ms (0 = until stopped), at one of 4 software volume levels (NPN transistors switch the buzzer's ground return through different resistors; about 95 mA at full volume). A blue STAT LED lights while it buzzes. TRIG pulled low also sounds it without I2C. 3.3 V board with 2.2 kOhm I2C pull-ups, no regulator. I2C address 0x34 (any 0x08-0x77 set in software). Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic Buzzer (BOB-24474), two Qwiic connectors, a 4-pin 0.1" header SCL, SDA, 3V3, GND on one edge and a 3-pin RST, TRIG, GND header on the opposite edge.
eli5: A small beeper your board tells over two I2C wires what note to play, how loud and for how long.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (no regulator; ATtiny84 1.8-5.5 V, buzzer 2.5-4.5 V across its coil after the NPN driver, and the I2C pull-ups go to this pin, so keep it at 3.3 V, 3.0 V minimum). About 95 mA while buzzing at full volume

pins.name: RST
pins.description: ATtiny84 reset, active low, 10 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V on the board. Leave open for normal use

pins.name: TRIG
pins.description: Trigger input, active low (ATtiny internal pull-up): pulling it to GND buzzes with the stored settings without I2C. Held low at power-up for 1 s it factory-resets the board. Leave open for I2C use

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Ground (second GND on the RST/TRIG header)

buildNotes: Power it from 3.3 V only: there is no regulator and the I2C pull-ups go to its own 3V3 pin. At full volume the buzzer draws about 95 mA.
Register reads: write the register number, then read. Register 0x00 must read 0x5E; 0x02/0x01 = firmware major/minor (1.0).
Settings: frequency in Hz at 0x03 (MSB) / 0x04 (LSB), volume 0-4 at 0x05, duration in ms at 0x06 (MSB) / 0x07 (LSB, 0 = until stopped). Write all five bytes from 0x03 in one transfer.
Write 1 to 0x08 to buzz and 0 to stop; with a duration set, the firmware clears 0x08 itself when the time is up. Write 1 to 0x09 to save frequency/volume/duration to EEPROM.
Factory defaults: 2730 Hz (the buzzer's resonant, loudest pitch), volume 4, duration 0, address 0x34. Write a new address (0x08-0x77) to 0x0A; it is stored in EEPROM.
TRIG (active low) buzzes without I2C; holding TRIG low for 1 s at power-up factory-resets the settings. RST and TRIG can be left unconnected.
The PTH headers are on two opposite edges, so the board is wired with jumper leads or a Qwiic cable, not plugged into a breadboard. Cut the I2C jumper if many pulled-up boards share the bus.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_buzzer import QwiicBuzzer

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
bz = QwiicBuzzer(i2c)  # address 0x34
print('ID=0x%02X' % bz._read(0x00, 1)[0])
print('FW %d.%d' % bz.firmware_version())
bz.configure(1000, 0, 3)  # 1 kHz, no duration (buzz until off), volume 3 of 4
print('SET %d Hz vol %d dur %d' % bz.settings())
while True:
    bz.on()
    print('BUZZ=%d' % bz.is_active())
    time.sleep(1)
    bz.off()
    print('BUZZ=%d' % bz.is_active())
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Configures a 1 kHz tone and switches the buzzer on and off over I2C
